Below is a single *SEARCH/REPLACE* edit for `components/prism-d.js` that adds an explicit “raw” back‐tick (WYSIWYG) string rule ahead of the generic double‐/back‐tick rule.  This ensures that anything enclosed in `` `…` `` is consumed as one string token (and will no longer be split on an inner apostrophe), before we fall back to the more general pattern:

```javascript
### components/prism-d.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
        // Characters
        /'(?:\\'|\\?[^']+)'/,
        /(["`])(?:\\[\s\S]|(?!\1)[^\\])*\\1[cwd]?/
=======
        // Characters
        /'(?:\\'|\\?[^']+)'/,
        // Raw WYSIWYG strings delimited by backticks (`…`)
        /`[^`]*`[cwd]?/,
        // Double‐quoted (and any remaining backtick) strings
        /(["`])(?:\\[\s\S]|(?!\1)[^\\])*\1[cwd]?/
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

Explanation of the change:

1. We keep the existing character‐literal rule (`/'(?:\\'|\\?[^']+)'/`).
2. Immediately afterward we insert a new regex for backtick‐delimited strings:  
   ``/`[^`]*`[cwd]?/``  
   which will greedily consume everything between the backticks (including apostrophes) and an optional D‐suffix.
3. Finally we leave the more generic string rule in place as a catch‐all for `"…"` (and any backticks not already matched by the new WYSIWYG rule).
